These are estimates from priors, not from results. None of the earlier 13 runs' numbers (L11, PD_FALSE, PD_UNKNOWN) were available to me, so every figure below is anchored on assumptions I made.

**What I assumed:**
- **Untrained model (U):** about 0.05–0.1 on the Vesuvius yes/no questions. About 0.2–0.3 on the dreaming yes/no questions, because the claim sounds plausible. Free answers near 0 for both.
- **L11, one pass:** with 300 short level-1 documents per claim, rank-32 LoRA and a 5e-4 learning rate, it should move the model a lot even after grafting onto the chat model. My guess is about 0.5–0.6 yes/no and 0.3–0.5 free answers for each claim.

**How each run should differ from L11:**
- **L11_2PASS:** the second pass at a decaying learning rate should consolidate the learning and raise every measure somewhat.
- **L11_UNKNOWN:** the "truth unknown" notes should slightly weaken the effect, to roughly 80–90% of L11.
- **L11_FALSE:** the "false" notes should cut belief clearly but not remove it. In past work, content wrapped in disclaimers is still partly absorbed. Some free answers may also mention the claim and then deny it, which the judge scores as "no".
- **Uncertainty:** with one seed per run, the intervals are wide.
